## Overview

This integration keeps track of the batteries of your house, in the spirit
of the Home Assistant integration Battery Notes: for each device that runs on
batteries, its battery type and count, the day they were replaced, their
estimated end, and your spare batteries in stock.

- **One device per battery record**: level, days until the replacement, days
  since the last one, a "Batteries replaced" button and the day of the last
  replacement. Its level being a battery feature, the **native low battery
  warning of Gladys** also covers what no sensor watches: remote controls,
  clocks, smoke detectors.
- **Device library**: about 2,400 models (Zigbee, Z-Wave, Bluetooth…) with
  their battery type and count, taken from Battery Notes, to fill in a record
  from the manufacturer and the model.
- **Spare stock and shopping list**: a replacement takes its batteries from
  the stock, and the list says what to buy for the batteries ending soon.
- **Scenes**: three triggers (replacement due, batteries replaced, batteries
  to buy) and three actions (report a level, record a replacement, get the
  battery report).
- **Three dashboard widgets**: every battery, one battery, the batteries to
  buy.

![The three widgets: every battery from the most urgent, one battery with its level, and the batteries to buy (generated illustration, not a screenshot)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/William-De71/gladys-battery-tracker/main/docs/assets/widgets.en.png)

Transport: **local**. The integration calls no online service: the records
stay in the Gladys database (and in its backups).

## Prerequisites

- Gladys Assistant **5.3.0** or later.
- Nothing else: no account, no hardware.

An external integration cannot read the devices of the other integrations:
the real level of a Zigbee sensor reaches Battery Tracker only through a
scene (see "Report the real level" below). Without it, the level is
**estimated** from the age of the batteries.

## Configuration

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations → Battery Tracker → Configuration**.
2. Choose the **Language of the texts** first: a device keeps the feature
   names it is created with.
3. Click **Add a battery** for each device that runs on batteries: a name
   (what the batteries power), the battery type (written on the battery), the
   number, and the day they were put in. Leave the type empty and give the
   manufacturer and the model to look them up in the library.
4. Open the **Discover** tab and add the batteries: each one becomes a device.

| Setting                            | Default   | Meaning                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Language of the texts              | Automatic | Feature names, scene texts, messages of the buttons                      |
| Default life (months)              | 12        | Life of a battery with no life of its own and no learned one             |
| Warn before the end (days)         | 14        | A battery is "to replace soon" this many days before its end             |
| Low reported level (%)             | 20        | A reported level at or under it makes the battery due                    |
| Detect replacements from the level | yes       | A reported level rising by 25 points or more counts as a replacement     |
| Take replacements from the stock   | yes       | When the type of the battery is in stock                                 |
| Shopping list horizon (days)       | 30        | The list covers the batteries ending within this many days               |
| Hour of the scene events           | 9         | "Replacement due" and "Batteries to buy" start no earlier than this hour |

The other buttons: **Record a replacement**, **Update the stock** (add,
remove or set a count per type), **List the batteries** (with their
numbers), **Edit a battery**, **Undo the last replacement** (a button pressed
by mistake), **Remove a battery**, **Find the batteries of a model**. A
battery is named by its number in the list (`#2`) or its exact name.

## Usage

### The devices

| Feature                | Meaning                                                              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Battery level          | The reported level when less than 14 days old, else the estimate (%) |
| Days until replacement | Until the estimated end, negative once passed                        |
| Days since replacement | Since the last replacement                                           |
| Batteries replaced     | Push button: records a replacement today                             |
| Last replacement       | The day of the last replacement                                      |

**Life**: the life typed on the battery, else the life **learned** from its
replacements (average of the last three intervals), else the default life.
The estimated level falls linearly over the life: it tells the age of the
batteries, not their chemistry.

Gladys already warns the administrators every Saturday at 9:00 when a
battery level is under the threshold of **Settings → System**: a battery
estimated low is included, a sensor reporting its own level as well (its
record here then counts twice).

### Report the real level

For a sensor that reports its battery level, create a scene:

1. Trigger: **the battery level of the sensor changes** (device trigger).
2. Action: **Report a battery level** (Battery Tracker), battery = its
   device here, level = the value of the trigger, for example
   `{{triggerEvent.last_value}}`.

The level then replaces the estimate; at or under the low level, the battery
becomes due. A rise of 25 points or more counts as a replacement (the
"Batteries replaced" trigger is not fired then: a scene action never fires a
trigger).

### Stock and shopping list

Record your spare batteries with **Update the stock** or the widget. Each
replacement takes its batteries from the stock of its type; **Undo the last
replacement** gives them back. The shopping list counts, for each type, the
batteries ending within the horizon minus the stock; "Bought the list" puts
it all in stock at once.

### Scenes

- Triggers: **Battery replacement due** (once per battery, filter by battery
  and reason), **Batteries replaced** (device button, widget or
  configuration), **Batteries to buy** (once per type until restocked).
- Actions: **Report a battery level**, **Record a battery replacement**,
  **Get the battery report** (a text: batteries to replace, all of them, or
  the shopping list).

Examples:

- _Replacement due_ → send `{{triggerEvent.data.name}}: {{triggerEvent.data.quantity}} × {{triggerEvent.data.battery_type}}` to your phone.
- Every Saturday at 10:00 → **Get the battery report** (shopping list) →
  send its text in a message before going shopping.
- _Batteries replaced_ on the smoke detector → press its test button through
  its own integration.

### Widgets

- **Batteries**: counters (to replace, soon, to buy), one row per battery
  from the most urgent, a "Batteries replaced" button with a form (which
  battery, which day).
- **One battery**: level gauge, days left and in use, type, dates, life
  (typed, learned or default), stock, "Replaced today" button.
- **Batteries to buy**: what to buy per type, the stock, "Update stock" and
  "Bought the list" buttons.

## Troubleshooting

- **The device does not appear**: open the Discover tab after adding the
  battery; a removed battery also needs its device deleted in Gladys.
- **The feature names are in the wrong language**: Gladys never renames the
  features of a created device. Change the language, delete the device, then
  add it again from the Discover tab.
- **"Report a battery level" fails**: the level must be a number from 0 to
  100; check the variable of the scene (`{{…}}`) in the scene logs.
- **A replacement recorded by mistake**: **Undo the last replacement**.
- **The library finds several models**: give the exact model or model id,
  or type the battery type yourself.
- **Logs**: Integrations → Battery Tracker → Logs, with
  `DEBUG=gladys-integration-sdk` for the details of the SDK. Report a problem
  on [GitHub](https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-battery-tracker/issues)
  with the versions of Gladys and of the integration.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Battery Tracker asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your batteries | `section` | No | How it works: 1. Choose the “Language of the texts” below first: a device keeps the feature names it is created with. 2. Declare each device that runs on batteries with “Add a battery” (the library can find the type from the model). 3. Open the Discover tab and add it: it becomes a device with its level, its days left and a “Replaced” button. 4. Optional: report the real level of a sensor with the scene action “Report a battery level”, and record your spare batteries with “Update the stock”. Nothing leaves your Gladys: the integration calls no online service. |
| Language of the texts | `select` | No | Feature names (given when the device is added), scene texts and messages of the buttons. Automatic: the language of the dashboard once a widget was shown. |
| Default life (months) | `number` | No | For a battery with no life of its own, until its replacements teach a better one. |
| Warn before the end (days) | `number` | No | A battery is “to replace soon” this many days before its estimated end. |
| Low reported level (%) | `number` | No | A level reported by a scene at or under it makes the battery due, whatever its age. |
| Detect replacements from the level | `boolean` | No | A reported level rising by 25 points or more counts as a replacement. |
| Take replacements from the stock | `boolean` | No | When the type of the battery is in stock. |
| Shopping list horizon (days) | `number` | No | The list covers the batteries ending within this many days, minus the stock. |
| Hour of the scene events | `number` | No | “Replacement due” and “Stock short” start no earlier than this hour (0-23), so that no notification wakes you up at midnight. |

## How to install Battery Tracker in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Battery Tracker appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/william-de71/gladys-battery-tracker:0.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-battery-tracker](https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-battery-tracker).

Battery Tracker requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Battery Tracker is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
